The Madness from the Sea Thurston’s Assembled Record (3 chapters) Narrative Chronological Ch. 1 — 1. The Horror in Clay — Thurston inherits his grand-uncle’s papers and finds a clay relief stored with notes headed “CTHULHU CULT.” Wilcox brings the relief to Angell and describes dreams of a vast dripping city and a pulsing voice. Wilcox’s delirium coincides with disturbed dreams, artistic frenzy, and strange outbreaks reported across the world. Thurston reconstructs the interviews, questions Angell’s death, and resolves to follow the evidence in the box. 4 scenes · 2,985 words Read to here Ch. 2 — 2. The Tale of Inspector Legrasse — Legrasse presents a captured idol to archaeologists in St. Louis, and Webb recognizes its likeness. Webb recounts an Inuit rite whose chant and image match the Louisiana object. Legrasse’s earlier police expedition follows drums and firelight to a ritual clearing beyond the bayous. A captured sailor explains the cult’s guarded tradition, its sleeping beings, and the conditions for their return. 4 scenes · 4,814 words Read to here Ch. 3 — 3. The Madness from the Sea — Thurston finds a newspaper report of the Alert, a dead crew, a strange idol, and the sole survivor Johansen. Johansen’s widow gives Thurston the sailor’s manuscript, which traces the Emma’s encounter with the Alert. Johansen’s landing party crosses the impossible city and opens a vast portal in its stone. Cthulhu pursues the survivors; Johansen turns the yacht upon it and carries the fatal knowledge home. 4 scenes · 4,169 words Reading here
